rulings_in_order: Ruling: Reuse verified existing local branch and implement locally verifiable E scope while tracking real environment gates separately — no Docker/kubectl or installed Python3.9/3.11/3.14 discovered; missing environment does not block packaging/manifests/runbooks — cost if wrong: offline completion can be mistaken for release approval, so release verification remains unsuccessful until mandatory external gates pass.
Ruling: Use PowerShell/Python bookkeeping in the exact plan-owned directory — Windows cannot run Unix helper scripts directly — cost if wrong: manual ledger drift; final review checks contracts.

Ruling: Offline wheel isolation shares explicit preinstalled dependency directories but not source paths; clean dependency resolution remains a failed/pending mandatory release check — no wheelhouse/network assumption — cost if wrong: offline smoke may miss dependency-install incompatibility; CI clean install remains required.

Ruling: Keep Python>=3.9 declaration and use SDK29 constraints on3.9, SDK37 on>=3.10, with compatible build tool pins — local SDK37 metadata requires>=3.10; no unavailable interpreter results are invented — cost if wrong: matrix may expose unsupported combinations before release.

Ruling: Allocate one RWO state claim per scheduled inspector profile — one shared RWO claim cannot safely attach across simultaneous jobs on different nodes — cost if wrong: more PVCs and storage, real CSI/restart/locking behavior remains pending.

Ruling: Bridge ingress policy is shipped; egress rules require actual CNI/API/proxy/DNS policy data — a universal Feishu IP whitelist would be misleading — cost if wrong: outbound confinement is not yet enforced; must be completed before real deployment.

Ruling: Runtime/build constraints pin selected direct dependencies/tools, and candidate metadata records actual resolved versions — cross-version clean installs are unavailable locally; no complete transitive lock is claimed — cost if wrong: later resolution may drift; clean CI/container evidence and recorded versions remain required.

Ruling: E4 verifier always retains failed/pending environment acceptance until actual operator-reviewed runtime/storage/receiver/shadow evidence exists — user explicitly selected offline preparation — cost if wrong: users expecting a release-ready green result must complete external acceptance later.

Ruling: Interpret source-isolated wheel imports by resolved installed module location, not substring exclusion of the entire project root — plan literal assertion rejects a valid ignored venv inside the workspace — cost if wrong: mixed-package leakage could be missed; root package and required submodule imports plus outside-source tests are exercised.

Ruling: Keep the existing local branch and checkout after offline handoff, without integration menu — there is no remote or distinct merge target, and user authorized continued local completion only — cost if wrong: owner must explicitly request later integration; nothing is pushed or merged.

Final: Ruling: Actual Python matrix, clean dependency resolution, Docker and published digest remain pending — offline user scope has no such runtime evidence — cost if wrong: package or image incompatibility may remain until real CI/build acceptance.

Final: Ruling: Server validation, CSI/locking/durability, CNI/egress, controller timezone and scale remain pending — YAML and local tools cannot establish target environment behavior — cost if wrong: volume loss, authorization or scheduling issues can still block deployment.

Final: Ruling: Real Feishu destination separation, credentials, provider behavior, shadow and cutover remain pending — distinct Secret names do not prove actual chat identity or delivery — cost if wrong: double or missing notifications until approved real receiver tests.

Final: Ruling: D collaboration and F standalone MCP/expanded checks remain outside E — existing fixed-group inspection release preparation is the agreed scope — cost if wrong: users expecting incident collaboration or MCP must wait for separate implementation.

Final: Ruling: Do not reopen unrelated A/B/C domain correctness in this E review — those batches have separate completed reviews; integration and recovery interfaces were examined — cost if wrong: unrelated latent defects may remain outside this release-preparation audit.

Final: Ruling: No complete transitive lock is claimed — current constraints pin selected direct dependencies/tools and actual resolved versions are recorded — cost if wrong: transitive resolution drift remains until clean installation and stronger locking are accepted.

Final: Ruling: Keep full release success=false without external acceptance and expose local CI status separately — a successful local validation subset must not certify production acceptance — cost if wrong: consumers confusing local exit status and release readiness may skip required gates; JSON/help document both.
